A.explanation: At A the field line is directed down and to the right from + to -, and the arrow is along the tangent but opposite to it, which is correct for a negatively charged electron with $F = -eE$.

B.explanation: At B the arrow points in the same direction as the field line leaving the + sphere, but an electron experiences a force opposite to $E$, so the arrow should be reversed.

C.explanation: At C the field is directed to the right toward the - sphere, so the electron force should be to the left along the tangent, but the drawn arrow is tilted away from the opposite tangent direction.

D.explanation: At D the field line points to the right toward the - sphere, but the arrow also points to the right, whereas an electron force must be opposite to the field direction.

hints: Notice the field lines are drawn with arrows from the + sphere to the - sphere - this is the direction of $E$, defined as the force on a positive charge.
Recall an electron has charge $-e$, so its force $F = -eE$ is opposite to the field direction at its position, along the tangent to the field line.
Compare each bold arrow to the tangent of the curved field line through A, B, C and D and keep only the one that points exactly opposite to the small field-line arrow.
walkthrough: Identify the field direction: electric field lines start on the positively charged sphere and end on the negatively charged sphere, as shown by the small arrows on the curves.
State the force rule: field direction is the force on a positive charge, so for an electron of charge $-e$ the force is $F = -eE$, opposite to $E$ and tangent to the field line.
At B and D the bold arrows point in the same sense as the field-line arrows, along the tangent toward the - sphere, so they show the force on a positive charge, not an electron.

At C the field line at that lower position is directed to the right toward the - sphere, so the correct electron force is to the left along the tangent, but the drawn arrow points left and upward off the tangent.

At A on the lower-left curve the field is directed down and to the right away from the + sphere, and the bold arrow is along the same line but up and to the left, exactly opposite to $E$. This is option A.
